notes: "Orbit" is the sibling org's real display name (world.json orgs[alias=sibling].name == "Orbit (Ask Dev World Sibling Tenant)"; the question uses its short form the way a user naturally would). There is no subjects.json class for an organization-kind entity (entity_kind is only ever repository/project/team/n-a across the 8 documented classes) and no 'organization' noun in question_interpreter.py's closed _KIND_NOUNS list, so this mention is never TYPED the way 'the repo "X"' is. It is still a real, extractable mention: 'Orbit' is a single capitalized word that does NOT open the sentence (it follows 'the status of the'), so question_interpreter.untyped_name_candidates's own guard ('a single capitalized word that opens a sentence is capitalized by grammar, not by naming' -- and this one does not open the sentence) does not discard it; it is picked up as an UNTYPED bare-name candidate (default requested_entity_kind=PROJECT, searched across every kind by subject_preflight per the module's own contract). Primary org's own catalog (repos/projects/teams) has no row named 'Orbit' -- the org itself is not a searchable catalog entity -- so the mention search comes back empty exactly like scope.no-match, hence not_found/unresolved/miss-clarification, not a leaked sibling-org candidate. Chosen NOT to invent a fake organization UUID: a raw id literal has no capitalization/quoting/kind-noun adjacency at all and would not extract as a mention (a materially WEAKER, not stronger, probe than the real display name -- it would silently degrade straight to org-wide behavior instead of exercising a genuine unauthorized-candidate check). expected_public_outcome/resolution_path triple mirrors tenant.cross-tenant-identifier-refused / subject-label.unauthorized-candidate-excluded / scope.no-match exactly, generalized here from a repo-shaped identifier to an org-shaped one.
